label: accel-slide-probe
_why: THE ANCHOR PROBE BEFORE THE ACCEL-SLIDE 2+1 (user-ruled 2026-09-21: "We'll probe first, and then run a full 2+1 run"). probe-accel-slide is probe-anch-costslide with ONE lever moved - the input ladder becomes the explicit per-era list 1 / 1.5 / 2.6 / 4.7 in place of geometric B 1.5^era - and its century batch (accel_slide_n2.json) costs ~6h. This 1836->1838 batch asks the one question a two-year span CAN answer: does the accelerating ladder wreck the 1836 anchor? The arithmetic says it CANNOT, and the probe is the falsification test of that claim rather than a measurement of the lever.
_the_null_prediction_and_why_it_is_exact: The accel ladder is IDENTICAL to the geometric one at ladder indices 0 and 1 (x1 and x1.5) and departs only at index 2 (2.6 vs 2.25, x1.156) and index 3 (4.7 vs 3.375, x1.393). Computed from the two emitted books against config/start_baseline.json: input VALUE moves on exactly 22 rungs, and NOT ONE OF THEM STANDS ON THE 1836 MAP. Every changed rung is e2 or e3; the only e2 presence in the whole 1836 start is tooling's 9 levels, and tooling is a SLID industry so its changed rung is e3, not e2. Per industry - food e2 only (map e0/e1), textile/furniture/glass/tooling e3 only (map e0/e1, tooling e0/e1/e2), paper/fertilizer/explosives/steel/motor/arms/artillery/art_academy e2+e3 (map e0, paper e0/e1), automotive e3 only (no 1836 presence). So F137's +27.3% anchor over-production is unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION, and so is every e0 and e1 recipe.
_what_this_probe_can_and_cannot_answer: CAN: whether the emitted book behaves as its arithmetic says at the anchor - world product, realised margins by era, which tiered types run negative and how many staffed levels they hold, and the British input-price path. CANNOT: the whole point of the lever - the frontier's margin, the hoard, obsolescence, the price decline - all of which need the century (ROADMAP step 10's standing warning, F142). A pass here is a GO for the 2+1, never evidence for the lever.

_arms.probe-accel-slide: THE BOOK UNDER TEST. config/mod_config.probe-accel-slide.json - A 2.2, the eight-industry e1 anchor slide, --anchor-cost, in0 1.2, C 1.9, ai_value 1000x3^era, the 10.75 defines, the 24-month bar, and the input ladder 1 / 1.5 / 2.6 / 4.7.
_arms.probe-anch-costslide: THE ONE-LEVER CONTROL, and the reason this batch is 4 runs rather than 2. It is the identical book on geometric B 1.5, so the pair isolates the input ladder exactly. It has NEVER been probed at this span - its only runs are the two century sessions 20260920_114003 and 20260920_170737 - so without it the nearest probed relative is probe-anch-in12 (20260919_190944), which differs by --anchor-cost as well and is therefore a two-lever comparison.

_delta: Between the two arms: `inputs` on 22 rungs and nothing else economic. `target_be` and `wage_pct` also differ, but only because probe-accel-slide is generated on the measured-wage basis of 2026-09-20 (10.87) while probe-anch-costslide predates it - target_be is emitted only into the building NAME and wage_pct is model-only, so neither is economics. building_cost, ai_value, the technologies, the defines and the tech-tree twins are identical.

_predictions._basis: The emitted books' own arithmetic (the zero-overlap census above) and the probe family of 2026-09-19, read at the same span and the same dump dates. Stated before launch, as the no-ceteris-paribus rule requires.
_predictions.world_product: PREDICT the two arms INDISTINGUISHABLE at 1836 and 1837 - within the 0.02 per-run spread the family shows - and both at 0.95-1.00 of the vanilla control. probe-anch-in12 read 0.98 / 0.96 at n=3 (per-run 408 / 407 / 406 at 1837), and --anchor-cost barely bites over 21 months because almost nothing is built (F142). ⚠ IF THE ARMS SEPARATE ON WORLD PRODUCT AT THE ANCHOR, the book is not what the arithmetic says it is, and that - not the size of the gap - is the finding.
_predictions.margins_by_era: PREDICT the e0 and e1 columns identical between the arms to within seed noise, near probe-anch-in12's e0 21% -> 26% and e1 29% -> 31%. The e2 column MAY separate slightly as the first e2 levels are built; e3 stays at zero on both (no e3 rung exists on the 1836 map and none will be built in 21 months).
_predictions.the_dead: PREDICT the same negative-margin set in both arms and no NEW e0 or e1 type in the accel arm - probe-anch-in12 read 1 of 21 types negative at 1836 (tooling e0, 7 staffed levels, 1% of tiered staffed levels) and 0 of 21 at 1837. A negative e0 or e1 type present in the accel arm and absent in the costslide one would be the falsification, because no e0 or e1 recipe differs between them.
_predictions.input_prices: PREDICT the British paths for fabric, wood, iron, coal, sulfur and tools within a couple of points between the arms. The accel ladder raises e2/e3 input demand, but there are no e2/e3 rungs on the map to exert it, so at the anchor the channel is closed and only opens as buildings arrive.

_go_no_go: GO for accel_slide_n2.json if the two arms are indistinguishable on world product and the dead set, and the accel arm sits in the family's 0.95-1.00 band against vanilla. NO-GO, and investigate the generator or the emission before spending 6h, if the accel arm separates from its one-lever control at the anchor, or if a negative e0/e1 type appears in it alone, or if world product falls below 0.90 of the control at 1837.
_comparison: The vanilla control and the canon in 20260919_132049_in0-early-probe (n=2 vanilla, n=3 probe-in12 = canon-c19-in12), and the mixed-anchor arms of 20260919_190944 / _193440 - all at this span and these dump dates. ⭐ NO VANILLA ARM IS RUN HERE: 20260919_132049 measured one on the same machine, game version, span and dump dates, so a slot spent on a second would buy nothing. That slot buys the one-lever control instead.
_instrumentation_note: The eleven tags and the six metrics of accel_slide_n2.json, not the probe family's seven and five, so this batch instruments EXACTLY as the century arm it gates (landmine L36's second half: a reference must instrument what the arms it is divided into do). The tag list is a SUPERSET of the control's, so the price basis intersects on those seven; of the four added, only BEL exists in 1836 - NGF, GER and UNL form decades later and will log nothing here, which is expected and not a fault. The dump dates are the probe family's unchanged, which is what keeps every 2026-09-19 arm reusable as a reference.
_watch: run 1 at ~3 min: the PM_TECH_REHAUL marker, the game version, the error window BY POSITION (not by a time-shaped pattern), the clock advancing
FIRST: whether the two arms separate at all - the whole probe is a null test
any negative e0 or e1 type in the accel arm that its one-lever control does not have
post-batch: preflight -Session, VERDICT.md, the SESSION_VERDICTS row, then launch accel_slide_n2.json on a GO
_cost: 4 runs x 1836->1838 at ~2.8 min of game each plus two builds and the harvest: about 18 minutes.
_caveats: TWO IN-GAME YEARS IS NOT THE CENTURY. Nothing here speaks to the frontier's margin, the hoard, obsolescence or the price decline - which are the entire reason the lever exists.
A NULL RESULT IS THE EXPECTED RESULT and is worth exactly what it says: the book emits what its arithmetic claims. It is not evidence that the lever works.

n=2 per arm. The arms are expected to agree, so a disagreement is the signal; but with n=2 a single divergent seed cannot be told from a real separation, and the answer to that is the century batch, not a third probe run.
building_cost is identical between the arms but --anchor-cost makes both differ from probe-anch-in12, so the cross-session comparison to that arm is two levers, not one.
Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30); the STOP file must be absent.

defaults._dump_dates_note: Identical to all six probe sessions of 2026-09-19, which is what makes every earlier arm reusable as a reference.

_run_order_note: Each arm's runs run BACK TO BACK, as the 2026-09-13 ruling requires and as every schedule of the 2026-09-19 probe family does. The book under test goes first, so a catastrophic reading on it can stop the batch before the control is spent.
